name: Croke Park
lore: Named after Archbishop Thomas Croke, an early GAA patron; the GAA's headquarters and national stadium since 1913.

name: Semple Stadium
lore: Named after Tom Semple, captain of the Thurles Blues hurling team in the early 1900s.

name: Pairc Ui Chaoimh
lore: Named after Pádraig Ó Caoimh, GAA Director-General 1929-1964; rebuilt and reopened in 2017.

name: Gaelic Grounds
lore: Limerick GAA's home ground since 1918, on the banks of the Shannon.

name: Fitzgerald Stadium
lore: Named after Dick Fitzgerald, Kerry captain and one of the game's first tactical writers.

name: St Tiernach's Park
lore: Named after Saint Tiarnach, patron saint of Clones; regular host of Ulster finals.

name: MacHale Park
lore: Named after Archbishop John MacHale of Tuam, a 19th-century Irish-language advocate.

name: Nowlan Park
lore: Named after James Nowlan, GAA president 1901-1921, a Kilkenny man.

name: Pearse Stadium
lore: Named after Pádraig Pearse, executed leader of the 1916 Easter Rising.

name: Breffni Park
lore: Named after the historic Kingdom of Breifne, which covered Cavan and Leitrim.

name: Dr Hyde Park
lore: Named after Douglas Hyde, first President of Ireland and a founder of the Gaelic League.

name: O'Moore Park
lore: Named after Rory O'Moore, 17th-century leader of the Irish Confederate Wars.

name: Cusack Park
lore: Named after Michael Cusack, a founder of the GAA in 1884; also known in Irish as Páirc Uí Chíosóg.

name: Pairc Esler
lore: Named after John Esler, a Down GAA official; shared with Newry Shamrocks GAC.

name: Markievicz Park
lore: Named after Constance Markievicz, 1916 Rising participant and first woman elected to Dáil Éireann; built in 1955.

name: Celtic Park
lore: Also known as Páirc na gCeilteach; Derry GAA's home ground in the city.

name: Athletic Grounds
lore: A multi-sport venue in Armagh city used by Armagh GAA since the early 20th century.

name: Wexford Park
lore: Wexford GAA's home ground since 1904, in Wexford town.

name: Brewster Park
lore: Fermanagh GAA's home ground in Enniskillen.

name: O'Connor Park
lore: Named after Dinny O'Connor, a local GAA benefactor; in Tullamore.

name: Healy Park
lore: Named after Bishop Eugene O'Doherty's predecessor John Healy; in Omagh.

name: MacCumhaill Park
lore: Named after Fionn mac Cumhaill of Irish mythology; home of the Seán MacCumhaills club, in Ballybofey.

name: Pairc Ui Rinn
lore: Named after Christy Ring, widely regarded as one of hurling's greatest players.

name: Fraher Field
lore: Named after Pat Fraher, a Waterford GAA administrator; in Dungarvan.

name: St Conleth's Park
lore: Named after Saint Conleth, patron saint of Kildare; in Newbridge.

name: St Mary's Park
lore: Home ground of Castleblayney Faughs GFC.

name: Austin Stack Park
lore: Named after Austin Stack, a 1916 Rising participant and Kerry footballer; in Tralee.

name: Cusack Park
lore: Named after Michael Cusack, a founder of the GAA; in Mullingar.

name: Dr Cullen Park
lore: Named after Cardinal Paul Cullen, 19th-century Archbishop of Dublin.

name: Walsh Park
lore: Named after Bishop Daniel Cohalan's contemporary; in Waterford city.

name: Pairc Tailteann
lore: Named after the ancient Tailteann Games, said to be held nearby; in Navan.

name: Pairc Sean Mac Diarmada
lore: Named after Seán Mac Diarmada, a 1916 Rising signatory born in Leitrim.

name: Fr Tierney Park
lore: Home of Aodh Ruadh CLG in Ballyshannon.

name: St Brendan's Park
lore: Named after Saint Brendan the Navigator; in Birr.

name: Parnell Park
lore: Named after Charles Stewart Parnell, 19th-century Irish nationalist leader; in Donnycarney.

name: Aughrim County Ground
lore: Wicklow GAA's home ground on Rednagh Road, Aughrim.

name: O'Garney Park
lore: Named after the River O'Garney; home of Sixmilebridge GAA club.

name: St Jarlath's Park
lore: Named after Saint Jarlath, patron saint of Tuam.

name: Pearse Park
lore: Named after Pádraig Pearse, executed leader of the 1916 Easter Rising.

name: McKenna Park
lore: Home ground of St Joseph's Ballycran GAA club.

name: Pearse Park
lore: Named after Pádraig Pearse; home of Arklow Geraldines Ballymoney GAA, in Arklow.

name: Corrigan Park
lore: Named after John Corrigan (1881-1916), Antrim County Board secretary; in Belfast.

name: Casement Park
lore: Named after Roger Casement, executed 1916 figure; traditional Antrim GAA headquarters, closed for redevelopment since 2013 (capacity is the planned post-redevelopment figure, not a current one).

name: Gaelic Grounds
role_note: Louth's home until 2020; new Dundalk stadium not yet open
lore: Louth GAA's home ground 1926-2020, in Drogheda; currently under redevelopment. A new stadium ("Staid Lu", 14,000 capacity) is under construction in Dundalk -- a different site -- and not yet open, so this row's bearing describes a ground the county is in the process of leaving.

name: O'Donnell Park
lore: Named for Cardinal Patrick O'Donnell (1856-1927); home of St Eunan's GAA club, in Letterkenny.
